panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power histological photomicrograph (2x) of an endometrial biopsy showing tissue with polymorphous inflammatory elements, consistent with malacoplakia as described in the article. B: High-power histological photomicrograph (20x) showing characteristic von-Hansemann cells with abundant granular cytoplasm and basophilic inclusions, pathognomonic for malakoplakia. C: Scanning magnification (40x) H&E showing rich histiocytic component (von-Hansemann cells) characteristic of malakoplakia, with an example indicated by a black circle. D: High-power histological photomicrograph (40x) showing macrophages (von-Hansemann cells) with accompanying eosinophils, consistent with the inflammatory infiltrate of malakoplakia.

(C) Scanning magnification of the previous picture shows the rich histiocytic component (an example is indicated by a black circle) intermingled between the tissue (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification 40x). in_text_mentions: The histological examination revealed the presence of infiltration of histiocytic elements with abundant granular cytoplasm and basophilic inclusions (so-called von-Hansemann cells), with accompanying polymorphous cells such as eosinophils, lymphocytes, plasma cells, and rare neutrophils (Figure 3). Furthermore, there were some areas of fibrosclerosis and no remnant chorionic tissue was observed. Immunochemical investigations revealed cells strongly tested positive for CD68 (PGM-1) and CD163 and negative for CK-pool.

panels.rationale: Renal biopsy histopathology (H&E) from a confirmed case of renal malakoplakia. The image shows sheets of histiocytes (von Hansemann cells) with inflammatory infiltrate, consistent with the in-text description of polygonal cells with abundant PAS-positive granular cytoplasm. The article title and caption confirm the diagnosis of renal malakoplakia. Michaelis-Gutmann bodies may be present but are not explicitly stated in the caption.
